I still haven't started my book even though I have been thinking about it for several days now. My brain is fixated on the mystery of Grandma. I am not saying that she is haunting me, but she is definitely on my mind and the fact that she got my brother to tell me she is proud of me has got me questioning everything. Was she sending me a message when I was going through a lot of old photos of hers and found that one? Was it a coincidence that a few hours later my brother was going to deliver the message from her? What really made her so mad back in 2010 when she stopped speaking to me for a year? Was it really the wedding thing or did something else upset her? And why did she sit on it for two whole months before getting angry about it? How does my brother know she is proud of me? Is he pulling my leg? Could this possibly be the apology I have been waiting on? I'm not sure how much I have written about her so I will sum it up. After living in Vegas for 14 years I wanted to move back closer to home. So, I quit my job, packed up my house and moved everything into storage and I flew out to my hometown to visit for two weeks and during that time I was going to do some job hunting, try to line up a few interviews and try to find a place to live. It was a big, stressful undertaking, but it was what I wanted to do so I was onboard. To save money I stayed with my grandparents for this visit. I decided I'd get some rest first then after a few days, I'd start setting up interviews and reaching out to potential places to live. While I was visiting I got invited to my ex-boyfriend's sister's wedding. I was really nervous about going for so many reasons. Should I go? Was it weird? Was it ok? I didn't know. I decided it was okay and I went. I then tried to come back to my grandparent's house at what I felt was an appropriate hour. It was before 11pm but it was after 9pm. When I walked in the house it woke my grandmother up and she came out from her room and interrogated me about where I was. She then went on to sternly let me know that she goes to bed at 8pm every night and my coming home late was not appropriate. She expected me not to do it again. That encounter had me so rattled and I felt terrible that I had woken her up that I couldn't sleep for the rest of the night. It was so upsetting that it kind of derailed my entire plan. The next day I went to my mom's and I never went back. I ended up couch surfing with my mom until I landed a job and I got an apartment. About two months later my grandmother calls me and screams at me and tells me she is done with me. I don't get it at all because we don't speak that often and I hadn't even seen her since that night. So, the only thing I can figure is something about the wedding set her off and she sat on it for about two months and then let me have it. I apologized to her over and over during that phone call. I tried to make amends and smooth things over, but she was SO angry that she didn't speak to me for a full year. I have never felt so hurt by anyone in my entire life. I still loved her despite this. When I have my feelings hurt I always want space anyway so honestly it was fine. Then about a year later she does what she always does and just calls me and starts talking to me like nothing ever happened. She never apologized to me. I told her about the apology thing 100 times but apparently it fell on deaf ears because she had no idea it was important to me. I have often thought maybe I should have pushed harder for it but anyway... it is what it is. She never apologized and I was hurt by it because I felt it was yet another thing that reinforced to me how unimportant I am to my family. My own grandmother didn't think an apology was important enough and on top of that maybe in her mind I didn't deserve one? I don't know. What I do know is you don't go an entire year not speaking to someone and then just act like it never happened without at least saying sorry. It changed me. It made me pull further away from my family than I already was. It hurts to feel disposable and worth so little. I didn't see her very often after that for the last six years of her life and when I did it was fine. It was just me doing my family obligation thing. When she died I was somewhat sad, but I felt like the hardest part was actually when she stopped speaking to me. That was when I grieved. That was when I really felt her absence. So, for my brother to randomly tell me she is proud of me is huge. I don't really know what to do with it. I want to believe he is telling the truth and it's not just something he told me because he wants to believe she really was proud of me. I don't know. I don't know how he knows. I mean I won't ask him because I know my brother. It would send him into panic and make him question his gut feeling and I don't want him to second guess himself. It just feels odd to now find out that maybe she was proud of me. When she couldn't even apologize for all the time we lost because she was angry with me because I..... I still don't even know why she got mad. I just don't understand why she would be proud of me either. But I will take it. Maybe she can see things from a more clear perspective now and maybe she now understands why apologizing is important? I don't know. I'm also finding it difficult to feel like this is over. It feels oddly anti-climactic. I wanted the apology so much that I would have dreams and fantasies about her giving me a real heartfelt apology. So because it kind of feels like she did that but didn't do it at the same time I don't know what to think or how to feel. Maybe I am reading too much into it? Maybe I should just accept what he said at face value and just know she is proud of me and that is enough. But.... What if she is haunting me?????? Kidding! ....kind of.

I did it! I completed a full year of daily journaling here. My entry count is 368, because I also wrote New Year's Eve last year, and I wrote twice on a couple days. I wasn't planning to journal every day this year - I thought it would be helpful through a stressful time, and then I just never stopped. I wrote 121,674 words this year, an average of 330 words per day. I wrote them in bed, on planes and trains and buses, in friends' living rooms and my parents' kitchen, in parks and parking lots and airport bathrooms. I feel really proud of maintaining this habit and the self-knowledge it's brought me. I didn't share all the hard things I've been through this year, but this was a place for me to slow down and reflect on them, and that's helped me get through it. Not just the tough things, but it's helped me notice and appreciate the beautiful, joyful, lovely things that made this year so rich. I was worried I'd run out of things to say or get bored with writing here, but that hasn't been my experience at all. It's still one of my favorite parts of the day. Thanks for being here and reading along. All the best to you in the new year.

I’ve just been thinking about how far we’ve come with acceptance of queer folk in my lifetime. I remember Ellen getting cancelled for being gay, I remember when Rosie O’Donnell came out as gay and everyone who had loved her that I knew suddenly shunned her and stopped watching her talk show. If you go back and watch Friends, they way they handled Ross’ wife being a lesbian was terrible.

When I first started teaching we had a principal who routinely said things that he thought were bad were gay, and when I said that made me uncomfortable (I was closeted) he laughed it off. People I worked with, not knowing I was in the closet, used to say things like “It’s fine if two men want to get married, but I don’t want to see them holding hands or kissing on Facebook. Some things are private” while of course thinking straight people holding hands or kissing on Facebook is fine.

When I came out on OD I had to let go of a friend/favorite because she told me that it was fine to be gay but I didn’t need to talk about it on my OD.

I mean it’s only been legal for me to get married for a decade.

And I just wonder . . . when will the acceptance of trans people come? It feels like trans hate is at an all time high. Katie can’t get a passport because they had the gender marker changed on their driver’s license and now the government won’t change the gender marker on passports, so now their passport and driver’s license don’t match. Just last year I had to let go of another LONG TERM PB friend/fave because she was going on about trans people and saying there should be laws about who should be allowed in bathrooms etc. And she used my discomfort with Katie’s transition as ammo against me which was super hurtful. And then there’s the whole trans athletes argument. And I just wonder why we can’t just let people live their lives the way they want to live them, so long as they aren’t hurting anyone.

There are definitely people who claim that trans people existing or using the bathroom is hurting someone, but there are also people who think that my relationship is hurting people/children, though it seems like a much smaller amount than there used to be. And I’m not sure if it’s generational or if some of the intolerant people have changed their minds.

To be honest, I was homophobic too, because that’s what I was taught. I didn’t think gay people should raise children. I was never even explicitly told what homosexuality was, just learned it from other children. I definitely was taught about trans people because my dad had a cousin who was trans, but in a very . . . immature way. So I don’t know if people have just woken up or what. But I am hopeful that things continue to progress, especially for trans people. Because even though I struggle with all of the changes my partner has gone through and the way that they chose to go about it was hurtful, it doesn’t mean I don’t think they shouldn’t have the right to do so.

Of course, we also need to work on our acceptance of black and brown people still and always. I just don’t get it. I don’t understand how you can look at ANYONE and think of yourself as better than them. I just treat everyone the same. And this isn’t an “I don’t see color” thing, because I understand that that’s actually hurtful, because you need to be able to see and recognize the struggles that BIPOC people face and if you don’t see color you will ignore that and your own privilege. But I mean I just treat everyone the same in regards to talking to everyone the same way and I definitely don’t think I’m better than anyone. I think most people are doing the best they can at any given moment, and that people are a product of their circumstances and the things that have happened to them. But I could never imagine dehumanizing someone enough that I could live with myself if I slapped a mask on and pulled them out of a car and arrested them for no reason.

I really do talk to everyone the same. People with disabilities, the elderly, and kids love me because of it. People who think they should be spoken to more reverently hate me for it. I have literally had conflict when I used to work because people didn’t like that I talked to the students the same way I talked to staff. The students loved me for it though. Especially the adult students in the moderate CI program. Because other staff would say “Hi JOHN, how was your WEEKEND?” in a saccharine voice and I would say “Hey John, what’s up?” normally to a twenty year old student. I even had coworkers tell me I didn’t have to talk to the students. One time I was making copies and on my way back, one of the adult students engaged me in conversation and was telling me all about Paw Patrol. And I knew nothing about Paw Patrol, so I was listening and asking questions. And his teacher said, “You don’t HAVE to talk to him.” Rude.

Obviously when I’m talking to someone with a cognitive impairment or developmental delay or whatever it’s called in your area, I’m going to approach it differently. But if I don’t know the person, or if I’m just socializing with them, I’m going to start normal and slow down or remove words if needed. There are definitely times where I’m like “Squash. Shoes. On.” Because I’ve tried asking him normally and his receptive language isn’t working well and I’ve boiled it down to essential words. But that’s not where I’m starting and I’m also still going to talk to him like a normal person, just with fewer words if he needs that accommodation. And at this point I do believe he has a cognitive impairment just because he hasn’t learned some things we’ve been working on for years and years. Not because the assessments said that originally, because standardized assessments assume that you have motivation to complete them and understand the social construct of asking and answering questions, both of which are things that many autistic people, and specifically Squash, are lacking.

Squash also is on the receiving end of that saccharine talk sometimes. He had a speech therapist that did it until I was like, “You can just talk to him normal.” He doesn’t like people who talk to him like that and can you even blame him? He’s 14 not 2!

I’m telling you, I’ve seen shit. I think 50% of people who work with people with disabilities are on a power trip.

I got off topic. But basically, we have come a long way in our acceptance of gay people. Now let’s work on accepting minorities and treating people with disabilities as competent people. Please and thank you.

They told DOGE their ideas, how to cut costs/save money, and DOGE said? "No. Fire them." Just like that. It's so stupid that almost a year later typing this out still brings me to tears, but damn if that doesn't sting. I'll never forget that they FOUGHT FOR US though. Never. My coworkers were sobbing as I consoled them and packed up my stuff. The job that took me 16 long years to finally get, and I lose it for the sake of a façade to present savings to the American people. I can't actually delve into details on my position because I still want to maintain complete anonymity, but enough departments, bureaus, and various types of staffing positions were eliminated that if I leave it there it's still okay. Suffice to say my positions was actually important, though. Most of them were, really. I'm sure there are some people in some places that might have been best replaced, but the key there is replacing because the POSITION is still important. Anyway, I consoled my colleagues as they helped me to my car with my stuff. Namely the mail cart we had to bring to hold all my plants. 😖 🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿 As soon as work hours were over, I got a text from my boss with a link to a lawsuit. Zero people wanted this to happen. Maybe elsewhere, but not in our office. We were valued. Really seems like a fairy tale job, eh? A job where you are respected and treated as a human and not a machine!? UNHEARD OF! Honestly, that was the first time I had experienced that. I was just shy of 40 years of age before I finally got this job… what was supposed to be my final job because I was not going to leave a place that let me leave at the end of the day without any stress or a sense of dread at the thought of returning. I was so happy to finally have my place. The next handful of weeks I spent struggling. I applied to jobs left and right, editing my resumes and cover letters for each, but only applying to things I realistically thought I could get. I also applied for food stamps, state medical coverage, and unemployment. Just over a month later my (former) boss called me to say they (boss + 2 higher ups) wrote us (fired employees) letters of recommendation to use, and please let them know if there is anything they can do or use them as a reference and they are sorry they can't get us back but they tried… I offered to come INTO office to pick them up since I was taking my daughter downtown for Honor Band practice anyway. It was an hour later. I showed up and THEY WELCOMED ME BACK. In that hour we were gone, a court determined it was illegal and my boss JUMPED at the chance to get us back in office ASAP. They said "a butt in the chair is harder to justify firing than one sitting at home". I got to go back to work the next week. I then had to pay back the unemployment I got (all like, 3 weeks of it), but I was happy to do such because I HAD MY JOB BACK! After 2 weeks it felt normal again. Well, normal minus having to report to DOGE every week with 3 things we did that week that were productive. I mean, I get wanting to verify productivity in the workforce, but nobody, and I mean NOBODY trusted them. Some people sent them with read receipts and would get notification they were deleted unopened. Some people responded with snark, like sharing mental health resources with colleagues due to the hostile work environment it has become. Those people got written up or fired. Thing is, they had algorithms. It didn't matter what you said, so long as you said something and it wasn't aggressive. This is my first real usage of AI: my boss showed me how to put in my job description, write briefly what I did this week, and then have AI write up a bulleted list of what I could report I did that week that would appease the assholes in power. My boss heavily encouraged the use of AI. Big proponent. I didn't really like it at first, though I've come around to appreciate it more. Still, it greatly simplified that menial task which actually was pretty daunting to someone that was just fired for supposedly "poor performance" while their supervisor kept telling them "you've been an exemplary employee; we didn't write this. We had no say in this." I appreciated learning how to speak to AI to get the results needed: it came in handy later. Not much later, actually, because after 2 weeks I was feeling settled in again… when word of the looming Reduction In Force (RIF) hit. Let's be real: this is a normal thing when new administrations come in, but historically we were not touched. We are different. We are more important, our role is vastly more critical than some, and while RIFs are common, they aren't to our bureau. I low-key thought, "yeah, I'll decide later whether or not I follow up on that…" But here's the thing: she also offered me HRT therapy for my perimenopause symptoms… which means I could maybe start sleeping better at night. Score! But, wait: you can't take hormones if you have a tumor. So she told me she wouldn't prescribe the HRT until we got the results of the MRI. So this was the dilemma: how bad did I want the HRT? Bad enough to schedule the MRI, it turns out. I knew it was going to be rough, and it was. I mentally prepared myself as much as possible for being stuck in a tube, not able to move, with very loud noises going on all around me… but I don't know how much it helped. They gave me headphones and put on some "easy listening" soft rock, but I could barely hear it because the machine was so loud. I can't breathe! Yes, you can. That's just your tongue sliding back into your throat. Push it forward. I can't breathe! Yes, you can. This is just your brain trying to panic. Ground yourself and take deep breaths. I need out now! No, you don't. You're fine. And if you move you're going to have to start over. I was eventually able to cope by counting and gently tapping with one finger. It worked against me once, though, when I tapped a little too hard and got a blurry image and had to repeat a scan. I kept track of time by counting songs. The scan only took 30 minutes, but it felt like an eternity. Halfway through they pulled me out and injected the contrast. I was shaking so they gave me another warm blanket. "Are you okay?" "Yup." Lies. I got through it, though. I should get results in the next 24-36 hours. I'm sure they will be clear, which is ultimately a good thing. It doesn't feel like a good thing at this moment. It was an expensive test in sensory hell and I was exhausted the rest of the day. But on the plus side I'll get to see what my brain looks like. Oh, and HRT. S.

A distant ex of mine used to accuse me of being 2% gay based on a phenomenon that she noticed back then, that many have noticed before and since: I hit it off with almost every gay man that I meet- no flirting, or fake bullshit- just genuine warmth and friendship. I hit it off similarly well with women who are exclusively into other women, assuming I have some kind of introduction from a trusted mutual. They're often more closed off and defensive, which I totally understand, no aspersions cast AT ALL there, but with guards lowered I find a lot of laughter. With women and gay men thoughts have a very chaotic fluidity to them, which churn and stir undescribed in this cloud between the two of us, obscuring objective meaning and allowing us both to draw whatever we wish to see from it, while still maintaining connection. A connection of pure feeling, with the specifics of how to arrive at that feeling somewhat veiled, necessarily. With men and gay women thoughts are crystal clear, and synchronized. It's the feelings that churn undescribed in a cloud between the two of us. It's an interesting dichotomy. I wonder if anyone else experiences this? I don't think it has much to do with why I get along better with gay folks than I typically do with straight folks, despite being straight myself. I think being an outcast is what makes that happen. Not directly. Not through camaraderie, but through an indirect mechanism of it. If there is one thing I, or any outcast I imagine wants, it's to be known and accepted. Known and accepted. Why? It's the only path to not being alone. The most telltale sign of an outcast isn't what you think. They aren't the people with their noses down lost in propaganda like you imagine. At least not most of them. The true sign of an outcast you can see immediately. Within 5 seconds of meeting them. Their eyes will be wide open, but soft. Not blank doe eyes, but not sharp predatory eyes either. Something in the middle. Something that feels mischievous, even though it isn't. It's just desperate openness. A full throated and constant willingness to be seen and known, completely compulsory based on a lifetime of not having it, and the inversion of fear that occurs in adulthood- from "what if they see me?" to "what if no one sees me?" I promise the warmest people you meet, the most generous and genuine, the most eager and willing to help types that you know- that you might think hold the world together- actually feel very far away from it, and everyone deep down.

I have a way with words. I didn't always. But for much of my adult life, I have known how to use language. I always knew the power of words, dating back to my childhood, but it wasn't until after I finished college and started using words, both spoken and written, in a professional capacity that I realized something very simple. My words have power. In general terms and when used properly, words indeed have power. I have known this for years. Earlier today, I lost someone I truly regarded as a friend, as someone with whom I believe I had an especially deep connection. I wrote about her in a few recent, previous entries. I was never afforded the opportunity to talk things out with her and reach some kind of understanding. It was my intent to keep our relationship intact (after someone here on PB had written me a comment on one of my entries, a comment that resonated with me and made me realize that this was a relationship worth fighting for) and move forward, but in the end, I have no choice but to accept this as a major loss. A very, major loss. I had the words ready. I knew what I wanted to say. I didn't rehearse what I was going to say or anything like that, but I wanted to give this a shot and see if we could patch things up. As I said, that opportunity never presented itself. She walked away before I could say anything. This entry will be dedicated to what I would have said to her, what I had building up in my mind for a good portion of the day, words that I never got a chance to say. You never gave me a chance. I know I said some things, things that you were quick to take at face value, without allowing me to elaborate further. Yes, I said that I don't rely on other people for anything, not for entertainment, not to keep me company, not to assure me that I'm not alone in this world. I did say that and I still stand by that. You knew from the beginning that like you, I am introvert. You being an introvert yourself is what attracted me to you in the first place. I liked being able to communicate and associate with and otherwise be a part of someone's life who I believed was like me in a way. Here's where your abrupt exit has led you to believe some things that maybe required additional explanation. You see, I don't rely on others for certain things. In some way, I don't need people. But in your case, I WANTED you to be around. I wanted you here. You came into my life and made yourself comfortable. I got used to you being here. I opened up to you. We opened up to each other. I came to accept you as a part of my life, as someone I enjoyed talking to and exchanging ideas, thoughts, and emotions. I saw you as a confidant. Without a doubt, you were someone I could talk to. Talking to you did not require any effort. It felt smooth, seamless even. It felt natural, like I could tell you anything. As you know, for an introvert, talking to others is NEVER that simple. Talking can be taxing, if not downright stressful at times. That was never the case with you. We had even reached an understanding regarding what you had said about my taking advantage of you. At least, I thought we did. You had told me repeatedly that I matter to you. Did I perhaps err by not telling you the same thing, maybe in a timelier manner? Obviously, with everything that I'm writing and feeling, clearly you matter to me as well. If you didn't, I wouldn't be writing any of this and I wouldn't be feeling the way that I do. You don't know how happy you would make me feel, just by communicating with me every day, as we would effectively spend our days together, albeit from afar. I knew that no matter where I was or what I was doing, you were always just a text message away. I had come to see my cell phone as my portal to you, an outlet to normalcy and even an escape from the nonsense that tends to plague me throughout the course of my day-to-day life. I never questioned this, but yes, you were always there. Contrary to your belief, you indeed made me happy. You were always a source of happiness. You don't know how every morning, I would get anxious as the 6am hour would steadily approach, because I know that exactly at 6am, I would text you, so simply... Good morning... Though I'd be awake for well over two hours by the time that text message would go out to you, it wasn't until I sent that text message that my day would officially start. Now, with the way that you walked away, I won't have that anymore. Rest assured that I will definitely feel this loss tomorrow when I return to work and I won't have you by my proverbial side. 6am will come and go and gradually, it will lose all the meaning that it once had for me. For you. For us. As an introvert, I have always maintained a small circle of people around me. I have always valued quality over quantity and for a brief moment in time, you were part of that circle. You were one of the few quality people I had in my life. I don't like it when people I allowed into my circle leave, regardless of reason. In fact, truth be told, I hate it. It makes me feel like I wasn't good enough as a person for them to stay. Yes, I will always point the finger towards me. It is MY fault that they leave. What did I do wrong for them to decide that being in this man's life just isn't worth it, at least, not anymore? You told me that I was never going to need you. You told me that I never needed your care and assurances. I will say this and I say this with all sincerity. I do. I don't know if that means much anymore, anything that I've written here. What I do know if this. Here I sit, writing in my journal here, effectively talking to a ghost. You decided to walk away from me and leave me here, with all of these emotions swirling around in my head. These words will eventually drift into the atmosphere, evaporating into nothing. You used to refer to me as your "machine". I never stopped you from doing so and after a while, I started to like it. It made me feel that I could do anything, so long as I had the battery for it. It had also reinforced this idea that maybe, just maybe, like a machine, I didn't have any feelings. I didn't need them. Now look at me. Feelings. Emotions. Sadness. Loss. The feelings are clearly there. I guess in the end, maybe I should have told you that I cared about you? I don't know if it would have changed anything, but maybe I should have said it? I blame myself and will continue to do so. We could have overcome this, but in the end, it wasn't meant to be. You walked away and did so without giving me a chance to say everything I've written here. Tomorrow is a new day. It will also be what I believe will be the first of many days without you. I guess in some way, I'll still be around and you know where and how to find me. I just don't believe that, at least to you, that I'm worth finding again. In The Wizard Of Oz, the Tin Man didn't have a heart. In the end, I wish that I didn't either.

I had the day off because I worked on New Year's Day. I should've had a quiet, easy morning. Instead I got up and went to the hospital to get an MRI. I know what you're thinking: an MRI on Sunday? That's weird. Yeah, I thought it was weird, too. I imagine they just have so many people needing to get tests that they just schedule through the weekends. I have a new primary care provider. She's an internist and a DO. I casually mentioned that I've been having problems with facial numbness and trouble swallowing. I got scolded for not going to the ER every time it happens, but honestly it happens A LOT. She mentioned sending me to get a brain MRI to rule out any tumors or lesions but emphasized that she didn't think it was likely an issue. I low-key thought, "yeah, I'll decide later whether or not I follow up on that…" But here's the thing: she also offered me HRT therapy for my perimenopause symptoms… which means I could maybe start sleeping better at night. Score! But, wait: you can't take hormones if you have a tumor. So she told me she wouldn't prescribe the HRT until we got the results of the MRI. So this was the dilemma: how bad did I want the HRT? Bad enough to schedule the MRI, it turns out. I knew it was going to be rough, and it was. I mentally prepared myself as much as possible for being stuck in a tube, not able to move, with very loud noises going on all around me… but I don't know how much it helped. They gave me headphones and put on some "easy listening" soft rock, but I could barely hear it because the machine was so loud. I can't breathe! Yes, you can. That's just your tongue sliding back into your throat. Push it forward. I can't breathe! Yes, you can. This is just your brain trying to panic. Ground yourself and take deep breaths. I need out now! No, you don't. You're fine. And if you move you're going to have to start over. I was eventually able to cope by counting and gently tapping with one finger. It worked against me once, though, when I tapped a little too hard and got a blurry image and had to repeat a scan. I kept track of time by counting songs. The scan only took 30 minutes, but it felt like an eternity. Halfway through they pulled me out and injected the contrast. I was shaking so they gave me another warm blanket. "Are you okay?" "Yup." Lies. I got through it, though. I should get results in the next 24-36 hours. I'm sure they will be clear, which is ultimately a good thing. It doesn't feel like a good thing at this moment. It was an expensive test in sensory hell and I was exhausted the rest of the day. But on the plus side I'll get to see what my brain looks like. Oh, and HRT. S.

Friday was a grocery shop day. I got a few things done at home, and then Wendy came over in the evening for a visit, which was nice.

Saturday was taking my mom to the grocery store, and then I finally managed to put my new office chair together after three days of it mocking me (and a week of sitting on a broken chair). It wasn’t actually that hard . . . it took about half an hour including the unboxing. So now I have a new chair. Right now, I’m just very conscious of the fact that it’s not my old chair. It’s a bit different ergonomically. The arm rests are maybe an inch lower, which doesn’t sound like a lot, but I feel the difference when I’m using the mouse (I typically have to rest my forearm when I use the mouse otherwise I get elbow issues because my body is stupid). We’ll see what happens, but I might put the armrests from the old chair on the new chair (the attachment holes look like they’re spaced the same), or you can get pads for armrests (which would raise the resting surface up a bit). I tried another chair with adjustable armrests (which would have eliminated this issue), but I didn’t like that chair (and it was more expensive). I’m also having a hard time getting used to the back rest, which is one of the mesh ones (it seems that almost all the reasonably-priced chairs have those mesh backs), so it isn’t solid like my old one and it’s upholstered back rest. So my back feels kind of stiff (or maybe the muscles are just tired from holding a different position) after I’ve been sitting for a while. The new one has more seat padding than the old one, so that’s good. Hopefully I’ll get used to it in the next week or so. It is returnable for up to 30 days, but I didn’t really find anything else in my price range that I thought would be better, so it kind of feels like I either get used to this one or I’m screwed. Hmph.

Funnily, I was sitting on the old chair on Friday when I heard something hit the floor. I thought that what snapped on the chair (inside the piece that attaches the back to the seat) was plastic. But I found half a bolt on the ground that had clearly snapped off the other half (the other half was still attached inside somewhere). So that’s kind of wild. It’s just too bad those bolts that snapped aren’t accessible because replacing the bolts would have been easy. Oh well.

This whole “having a different chair” thing (especially when I’m not sure if my body will get used to it) just makes me feel stressed out. I’m not a fan of change. I sit in a lot of different office chairs at work, and some definitely leave me stiff by the end of the day. And sometimes I find myself thinking “thank goodness I get a different chair tomorrow). Well, with this new chair, it’s here to stay. And if I end up not liking it, I don’t know what I’m going to do. Perhaps I need to train myself to sit up straight without really using the back rest. I used to do that when I was younger because my physiotherapist told me strengthening my back so I could sit without leaning on the back rest would help with my jaw issues. So I used to be really good with sitting up straight. Perhaps this chair will force me back into that. 

The weekend’s other big chore has been taking everything out of my utility room and piling it up in my living room. I dislike the visual chaos of all that stuff in a place it shouldn’t be. It’s why unpacking after I moved here was so stressful - I just wanted all the Stuff put away so it wasn’t Everywhere. At least this is less stuff for a shorter amount of time. Next week, a technician is coming to clean all the dryer vents in the building, so we have to give them as much room as possible to work (our utility rooms are pretty tight). Most of my stuff is in storage containers, but I do have a small shelving unit in there as well, so that took a bit longer. 

But the biggest issue was something else. One of the previous owners built a makeshift cabinet that created a shelf above where the dryer hose connects to the building’s vent system - a fairly solid wooden box (with openings cut to slide around the dryer hose) which was cobbled together with various bits of cabinetry, panelling and scrap wood. It allowed more things to be stacked in there because the dryer hose does snake along a few feet of floor (which the shelf let you pile stuff above). I had to remove the box (that connection between the hose and the outlet would have been completely inaccessible otherwise), and it partially broke in the process. Additionally, inside and behind the box was so filthy with dust, dryer lint and assorted dinge that I just about gagged. Like that thing was either a health hazard, a fire hazard, or both. And that’s not even taking into account the random nail heads that were sticking out of it. I’ve never really been happy with having my stuff piled on top of this platform (which puts some restrictions on where you can put things). So I decided that this was a sign from the universe to finally deal with getting a proper storage solution for that corner. It’s money I don’t want to spend right now, but I was so disgusted by how much filth had accumulated, plus the box was partially broken in a way that reassembling it would have been difficult (and possibly leaving the box not as structurally sound). So today, I went scorched earth and completely demolished the thing. And that was quite a chore. I took almost 30 screws out of it, pulled out a whole bunch of nails of different sizes, and still had to go at it with a hammer and body weight to break it apart because it was also glued to high heaven. At one point, I was standing on one foot inside the box and using the other foot to push on the side to break the two pieces apart. The front appeared to be a cabinet door (that was still attached to another part with hinges. I made a huge mess in my kitchen (which was the best place to take it apart) and had to do a big clean-up operation afterward. 

I now have a box full of these panels and strips of wood that I have to take downstairs in a few shifts. We don’t have direct access to the dumpster, so I just have to leave pieces outside the utility room where the dumpster is. And I don’t want to leave the whole pile at once because the condo board might come after me for not disposing of my own “building materials” (there is a list of things we’re supposed to remove from the premises to dispose of due to size, and building materials is one of them). But if I just put a piece or two down there every few days, hopefully our caretaker just shrugs and tosses them in the dumpster.

Anyway, now I have to buy a utility shelf. I can assemble it such that the dryer hose threads through it so that I can use that vertical space that I don’t have on the floor. But because I have two very large storage totes that won’t fit (and there’s nowhere else to put something that size, in the utility room or otherwise), I’ll have to get some new storage totes as well and reorganize the stuff in the big totes (those big totes are started to get some cracks, so they would have been replaced soon-ish anyway). More surprise expense. Life loves throwing me surprise expenses around the holidays. GRUMBLE. 

Also, I need to leave a note on my dryer saying something to the effect of “Hello, if you have to move the laundry appliances, please make sure that when you put them back, both appliance doors are able to fully open without hitting the furnace.” Because there’s literally a centimetre of clearance right now, and if those machines aren’t put back properly, I’m certainly not capable of moving them myself.

So now let’s take that storage stress (and expense) and add it to the chair stress (and expense), and this is why I don’t want to go back to work yet.

This may not be the most exciting entry for anyone, just plotting things out in writing!

I’m about to have a bunch of “alone time” when my husband goes back to work tomorrow. Usually, I enjoy the time I have to myself, being a pretty serious introvert and also just one of those people that doesn’t really feel loneliness ever, no matter what the circumstances. I do, however, really enjoy the time that I spend with my husband. I don’t wish for alone time when we are together. I will not feel lonely tomorrow, but I will definitely miss him while he is gone and look forward to his return, as always.

That said… I’m about to have a bunch of “alone time.”

I have some new year things to do. We rearranged the house. I have no idea if I’ve written about that here yet. It feels like I have, but honestly, everything about this last few weeks has been a bit of a blur.

I’ve felt a bit lost.

I’ve felt a bit like I’ve been finding myself.

I’ve felt a bit like I should be doing things that I’m not doing.

I’ve felt frustrated by my body.

But whatever. Here I am.

(Pain doesn’t kill you apparently.)

Anyway, we rearranged the house and put the couch and TV downstairs again. It may only last the winter, but I’m happier with the arrangement already. It makes the space feel more spacious and less wasted. We have both our desks in the dining room. I’m sure I’ve said all this before now. Ha. Whatever. It’s my space. I’ll say it 40 fucking times if I need to. Maybe when I start saying things 40 times and not remembering, I (or someone) will pick up a pattern and I’ll be off to the memory care center.

You know, I didn’t imagine I’d still be writing at this age, all these years later. I didn’t not imagine it… it’s just a thing I didn’t think about as evolving. As if I’d feel like a different person throughout all these stages. As if I’d pick up and leave off so many times. As if I’d be so changed (and yet also, so same) every time I picked back up. Or that I would talk about that 40 fucking times. All the versions of me.

Again. Whatever. Here I am.

(There, there. “You’re here now and that’s all that matters,” the diary says to me.)

I leave voices here, don’t I? Do exiles live here somewhere? I’m sure I will find them in my backwards quest. That’s definitely something I want to get done. The importing process. The analysis. The pattern recognition.

I will now take a moment to bitch about how I crave routines and habits, as I do every new year. No matter, though. I will just rail against them with all my might. I will go down fighting with every justification that comes to mind.

(Have you ever thought that perhaps you are just not that into routines and habits? Have you ever thought that perhaps you are, at heart, more of a spontaneous type of person? Have you ever considered that maybe you only try and inflict this upon yourself because it is some sort of expectation that you imagine is upon you? Have you ever considered that maybe nobody actually cares and you should just do you?)

I was going through the importing a year at a time. But now I think that I might go back to importing them by the days and then I would be done in a year’s time. By that I mean, when it’s January 4th, and I write, then I would also import every year’s January 4th (at least the ones that aren’t already here. By doing that, I could have the whole thing done in a year. Of course that brings me back to habits, doesn’t it? The issue I ran up against is that I don’t reliably write every day. Days would be missing. The whole import would not get done.

Maybe if I took the pressure off myself a little? Maybe if I just sit down every day and write something. Anything, really. If nothing else, just a single sentence that sums up the day. Then import the old stuff.

I’m already exhausted with this day. And with thinking. And with new years. And with everything.

I might be having some separation anxiety. Or I should say I’m pre-panicking about my husband being back at work tomorrow. Ha. I’m really just so ready for us to be retired and be able to do our own thing together. I know that in reality, the years will pass quickly. Honestly, I’ll probably be looking back going, “What the fuck was I thinking, willing six years to pass quickly when I have so few years of my life left?” I do know they’ll pass fast.

I mean, just this diary importing thing is showing me how all of these entries seem like yesterday. When I’m going through pictures, I can’t even believe that some of them were taken 5, 10, 15 years ago. Didn’t that just happen? Didn’t we just go there? Don’t I still have that sweater and love it? Aren’t our cats still just tiny baby kittens instead of coming up on five and six years of age? A third or so of their lives gone? I hear songs playing and my husband says, “Guess what year this was,” and I’m honestly afraid to say. Was it yesterday? Was yesterday the year? Because that’s what it feels like.

It’s not that I even care about being or getting old. I mean, whatever. Time is a thing. Nobody has much choice in that no matter what we do. Eventually we’re all back to dust. It’s not the aging that is the issue. I mean, some parts of that, like losing my mind or my ability to move or maybe see or hear are frightening prospects. It will be dealt with, though, as it has to be. I think it is just the loss of time.

I mean, when it comes down to it, it’s really just that. It’s that I’ve lived so long and yet so few bits of my life were spent doing what I really want to do. What I enjoy. So much of it has always been in service to someone else, allowing them to extract as much as possible from me. It comes down to that thing I always say about how we could be lounging on beaches, eating fruit, making love, making art, helping each other and building things that we all share… but instead, we chose this. This is the society we built. This is the way things work. This is the system.

It’s so fucking gross. I saw a quote the other day that said something like… “Think about the reason why we have child labor laws. It’s because, if they could, they would extract everything they could even out of your children.” They would take the best years of your child’s life, too. They would pay them even less and treat them worse because they’re children and have less “rights”, too. (I’m sure it would be just one more way that fucked up adults would try to gain access to violate childrens’ bodies, too.)

I feel like in some fashion, the way I am living now is just me trying to shrink myself as much as possible so that nothing more can be extracted from me. Hide myself. Shield myself. Protect myself. Reserve my energy. Save my space. Steal back my time. Right a wrong or find my own kind of justice. Fix all the things that broke in me. Try to imagine possibilities for the end of my life as if there are some. As if I could make wishes like that and they’d come true. Like I could make decisions like that and they’d come true. Like decisions and wishes are made of the same stuff. Kind of feels that way, sometimes.

Fuck it. Just fuck it, you know?

Laurie has been cleaning rooms at the Holiday Inn for approaching sixteen years now. She is single, lives in a house with a broken railing on the deck and a yard that is rarely mowed. She owns a 1980-something Tercel that has not moved out of her driveway in the years I have known her. We take her to and from work ten times a week, 645AM for her morning clock-in and 330PM after her clock-out. The blue fabric of her uniform is always freshly pressed when she gets in my cab and she always carries about the aroma of laundered cotton. Her body is cute in the way a pug is cute, a sturdy muscular waddle underneath a flattened nose. She is always chatty and sweet, knows all the drivers by name. Despite that she is likely a minimum wage worker or close to it she always tips four or five dollars on an eight dollar fare.

When I first got to know Laurie I was concerned about her extreme friendliness, her interest in my thoughts and goings on and her overtipping. She would certainly not be the first to be overwhelmed by my charms so I resolved to maybe have a word with her about the extra money she was throwing at me, tell her I appreciated her generosity but it was unnecessary. Good thing I spoke with the other drivers about her before I did that because I found out she behaves that way with all of us. She is reluctant to speak about herself but I know she has a pair of cats. Word is she has never had children or a lover, nor expressed a desire for either.

Laurie takes the same ride every day from home to work again with the exception of Friday evening. On Fridays, she likes to make a stop at the local NSLC on the way home where she will buy a bottle of vodka to provide some weekend cheer. A quick stop, spirits obtained, we deliver her back home and we are awarded with a particularly large tip. On this particular Friday, I was assigned to take her home and I headed toward the liquor store without being directed to do so. We were happily discussing the weather when she told me that liquor store would be her final stop. “Are you sure?” I asked. She nodded in the affirmative, assured me that she had some errands to run. She got out of the cab and limped footsore into the liquor store after a hectic Friday shift.

It occurred to me a few minutes after I dropped her off that she might not be honest with me. She may have reviewed her wallet and discovered she would not be able to get home with the bottle and still give us her customary tip. I picked up the mic on the radio and shared my suspicions with the other drivers. I’d already accepted a ride elsewhere, so I could not circle back to follow-up. Lyn happened to be downtown so she scanned the sidewalks for Laurie and found her there, slowly limping home with a brown bag under her arm. Lyn told me later she pulled beside her on the sidewalk, gave her a dirty look and said, “Busted!” Lyn made her get in the car. Apparently it took some cajoling but Lyn got her in the back seat and gave her a free lift home. “Never do that again,” Lyn warned.

Roy is an old man now, likely topping his seventieth cycle around the sun. He used to work for us for the better part of two decades as a second career after sweating away three decades on the production floor at the tire manufacturing plant. His life as a cabbie came to a sudden end one morning when he woke up mostly blind. A visit to the emergency room revealed that he had a detached retina. Likely surgery the doctors said, a hasty trip to a specialist in Halifax was arranged. By chance I drew Roy as a ride several times taking him to the hospital in Halifax, a service provided by the public health authority. He was typically accompanied by his granddaughter, a sixteen year old hellion named Mikayla. Roy’s family history is a tale of one tragedy after another. Roy is raising Mikayla because the girl’s mother is off in some other city living off of heroin and fentanyl. She has not been seen in years and it is possible she is dead. Mikayla seems bent on a similar track. She is impossible to control, especially by a half-blind 70 year old. With Roy no longer available to drive he began to rely on one of Mikayla’s boyfriend/dealer, whatever he is to do basic errands. They live in a cold little hole on the side of a hill some twenty minutes outside of town. This arrangement worked about a week before the boyfriend totaled the truck, hit someone and hurt them. He was not insured in any way.

Roy was never my favorite human being when he worked with us but we got along. He drove nights while I manned the day shift so I seldom saw him other than to pick him up for his night shift or take him home when I started in the morning. He could be kind of a dunce and he was often paranoid of passengers and other drivers stealing from him. Ours is a cash business. Roy would nap in the cab stand at the end of his shift flush with his earnings. He said bills were disappearing from his pockets and initially suspected his coworkers rifling his pants while he was sleeping. I think it more likely he’d go home exhausted, fall into bed and Mikayla would roll him while he was passed out.

One morning I waited patiently outside of Sobey’s while Roy was inside picking up some items. Groceries are outside of the purview of the medical rides his family has been awarded but I take some uncompensated mercy on the man because it seems no one else will. Mikayla is balled up in the back seat of my cab sleeping in an impossible yoga-like position. Her hair is dirty and disheveled. She and her grandfather have not slept, bathed or eaten although they’d spent the previous night in a modest hotel near the QEII Hospital in Halifax at taxpayer expense.

Roy returns with a bag of groceries and lays it down in the floorboard next to a half-dozen white bags of pharmaceuticals just picked up, again uncompensated, from the nearby pharmacy. Roy is very short, likely 5 ft 4 or so and recently fitted with a black eyepatch. He is for all the world a very fragile looking pirate without dirk or dagger. He takes his place in the back seat with Mikayla and I pull out to the street. There is a low volume conversation between the two and at first I could not make out their words. “They did not have it,” he kept saying to her. For likely the first time ever, I heard her speak, her voice shrill and high-pitched. “What does that mean they don’t fucking have it?” she screeched. “You had one fucking job you fucking moron.”

I look in the rearview mirror and she is up on her knees, towering over him. He has one hand out defensively, his black eyepatch askew from his brow exposing the bandage underneath. “I NEED A PREGNANCY TEST, THEY HAVE FUCKING PREGNANCY TESTS!” she screamed over and again. In her rage she started to hoke up mucus to spit on him. Alarmed, I tap the brakes, pushing her off balance from her haunches. “Aint no way,” I say to the rear view mirror. My warning brings her back to earth and she returns to her seat, murmuring once in a while about how stupid her grandfather. A long tense ride to their cheerless hole south of town and I pull into the drive. She springs from the backseat and into the house. Roy apologizes to me. He says she is not eighteen yet but she will be soon and after that things are going to change. I tell him this is none of my business but he should talk to someone, get some help out here.

When a employee has a bad spell it is customary for Sheryl to take up a collection, buy a Sobey’s gift card and send it along to whomever suffered the disaster. A poster was put up to invite donations and I dropped off a ten at the end of my shift. I asked how much they’d taken in so far and was told my contribution brought it to only $35. Usually, these collections are quite large and for some reason few were contributing. Asking around, I was told Roy was not the most popular guy. Drivers did not appreciate his accusations we were stealing from him and most thought anything we contributed would be stolen by his progeny. Last but not least, I was told on the downlow, Roy was a man who preferred the company of men. If I had been told Roy was an astronaut I would be less surprised. Because of this, there was some doubt whether Mikayla’s mother was fathered by Roy. “You mean he volunteered for this shit?” I asked. “Yup,” I was told, “either cuck or fairy, no one knows for sure.”

January brings two looming worries for me. One is taxes. Will we owe? Probably. But how much? One silver lining of this administration is supposed to be taxes. A boring and irrelevant topic for most people, but my job hangs in the balance. Cuts would have to get really bad before I start worrying about actually losing my job, but it’s not completely out of the question. A more likely scenario would be that they would nudge more highly paid older employees into early retirement plans, which could sweep up my boss and one of my coworkers, turning our team of four into a team of two. And given morale is already souring under the modest cuts they’ve made so far, it could trigger some to flee what they see as a sinking ship. Even if my job is safe, it could change. A lot.
